review_text: I really loved the overall setup, aesthetic, and cleanliness of this place. The environment makes it a great spot to sit down and unwind. That being said, the food was a bit hit-or-miss. It fills you up and isn't bad by any means, but it definitely needs a bit more seasoning and personality to match how great the venue is. It's worth a visit for the location alone, but there is room for improvement in the kitchen.

Dear Joe Coffee Shop is a hidden paradise! The lush green surroundings make you feel like you're in the middle of a paradise, offering a serene and refreshing ambiance. While the prices are on the higher side, every sip and bite is worth it—everything tastes amazing, from the coffee to the food. The beautiful setting and quality experience make it a perfect spot for a relaxing escape!

Frequented this place and I must say the interior really gets to you —- the cleanliness, furniture, greenery, and music all just came together exuding a homely atmosphere. Garlic noodles with cajun shrimp and mint mocha frappe were savory. The Vietnamese latte, chicken toast, truffle cream chips were quite filling on a lazy and drizzling brunch. Rates were a bit on the higher side especially with the food. But good thing the drinks were at par with the other coffee shops. Some plates with meager serving sizes, some even more generous. Parking slots at the sides. Nice ambience, kind staff, and hardly people in the mornings. A place you'd like to visit again and again. And of course bring some friends too.
The atmosphere is really great! I can spend hours here reading a book or just talking to a friend over a good drink and food. Their chicken pie is an absolute must-try!

I adore this area so much! Though a little costly, the food is excellent. It's the perfect place to host meet ups or spend time with family (with older kids). There is plenty of space for parking in the restaurant's back.
I really love the ambience, with classy and natural interiors. I ordered Hazelnut Frappe 10/10 for me, and their Chicken Taco Salad is tasty 😋

Very good place to hang and chill. Enjoyed spending some quiet time here both alone and with company. Yuzu Raspberry and Lemon Blueberry cake are sooooo good! Double beef bolognese pasta was okay but loved that the serving can be enough for two people if you're not too hungry. It's pretty pricey but I love the ambiance enough to keep me going back

The shop offered a cozy, inviting atmosphere with comfortable seating and soft lighting. Awesome plants! 🌱🪴🎋 The shop employs friendly and helpful staff🤩⭐️, making us feel welcome. Personally, I preferred the pastry over coffee.

Ambiance was good. It was a refreshing cool cafe idea. Nice ang environment kay they integrated a warm woody feel with industrial modern look. Naa pod plants which make the atmosphere feel like you are in a jungle or close to nature. However, makacomment ko sa price. Kay ang artisan tea makapalit nag 4 cups sa regular coffee shops. Though it was good, I cant complain sa quality. But for occasional visits, it's definitely a place to chill and hangout.

we love their creamy carbonara. i also love their quesadilla except for the sauces. we also ordered the almond crusted fish and shrimp (i expected the shrimp to be sauteed but as you can see from the video it was just a commercialized steamed shrimp, the almond was just a small amount mixed in the flour); and the black pepper beef which i preferred more than the fish and shrimp. their matcha latte was more on the milky sweet side which i preferred less. i also like their vietnamese latte. will surely comeback to try their other pasta and pizza.
Great atmosphere, a bit pricey but I did enjoyed my time there. Coffee is really good. Not to many vegetarian options.

Garcia Road, Buhangin The first letter-writing cafe in the Philippines is now in Davao City! 💌📮They have a lot of options for rice meals, pasta, sandwiches, pizzas, and hot and cold drinks. ♦️ Hot Americano Tall - Php 165 ♦️ Hot Chocolate Tall - Php 180 ♦️ Iced Matcha Latte Grande - Php 215 ♦️ Tuna Melt Sandwich - Php 270

Dear Joe serves a pretty good cup of Joe. We ordered their Americano and Hazelnut Frappe. These were great with the Chicken Fajita appetizers. The place itself has chill vibes. The wifi they provide is snail-paced, so better bring your own pocket wifi.
The items in the menu are very expensive. But I like how they talk about and tell their customers who is "Joe". Also, you can write what you feel and put them inside the Letters to Joe box.
Loved the place it's so cozy, the food and coffee is great. Also i like the decorations inside the establishment specially the wall paintings.

The place is very nice with some wall beautiful murals. The place feels warm, cozy and inviting. You can write some love letters and seal it with wax. Very interesting concept. Coffee tasted good as well as the food. The service was a bit off though. The place was attended by two staff. A well uniformed but aloof lady and a guy in casual clothes with the left of his pants raised to the knee. Quite a strange duo.

I always enjoy my time at dear joe! Such a unique ambiance as well perfect if you're looking for a working space. I love their fruit shakes too, the mangoes they use are always fresh and when it comes to the food their truffle sandwich is a must try!

Smoked BBQ CHOPS Tuff. The meat was not hot. I believe precooked, frozen or refridgerated then microwaved. Was a let down. Had pizza before not crazy for, swore would not return but here i was again learning my lesson. Had watermelon which was to be 100% juice but was watered down with ice and some sugar. Disappointed 😞 for sure. Didnt drink it.
Nice interior but slow service and expensive food and drinks. They advertise their letter-writing but there were no papers and writing implements for writing and sending letters.

The place is huge and it offers a lot of meal options from simple Filipino snacks to Italian-inspired pastas. Their espresso doesn't stand out much but the ambience is good and the crew are hospitable. However, the coffee experience for dine-in customers could be better if the coffee and even the tea will be served NOT in a paper cup. The paper cup ruins the over all experience and doesn't justify the premium price that the customers payed for their tea and coffee. Please heed this request.

Basically you just come here for the place because the interiors are nice and aesthetic, perfect place to be seen and for posting in your social media. I couldn't say the same for the food. It is super expensive, even for Manila standards. The taste is only so-so and the portion size not commensurate to the price. The staff takes so long to take order. I understand that the place is newly opened but shouldn't be an excuse to be fumbling around the register to punch. Once is enough to visit and to experience the "feel" of this place but not worthy enough that you would keep coming back.
Ambient-wise it is a perfect place for going solo and group meeting/study. Or just having "ME Time" .

As someone residing in the southern area of Davao City, the coffee shop was a bit far, but luckily, I visited during a holiday. I ordered coffee and cheesecake, both of which were good (not the best but decent). Items jb the menu were a bit more pricey as compared to other local coffee shops. The ambiance of the place was pleasant, and I couldn't help but notice that its menu and ambience were quite similar to Coffee Project, which makes sense since both are owned by the same conglomerate.
1 star for listening yourself on gmaps as open when you're not. At 8am on a Sunday. Drove across town to visit for the first time. Not open.
It's so amazing. You can drink iced coffee made with tap water at an expensive price. Are you saying you lack expertise and conscience?

Finally, a good coffee place in Davao, that opens at the right time, has a good ambience, good coffee machinery, and actually good coffee. Should have a bit more variety of beans selection is my only critique. But hey, this is a great start and I will patronize it as my local cafe. Keep up the great work !

OMG If you thought Starbucks was expensive don't come here! The coffee wasn't bad but id rather go to Starbucks and pay 40 pesos less for a better product. I didn't try the food - I didn't want to spend that much and be disappointed again 😭 Here is the wifi password that doesn't work. Why do Filipinos make the simple things so damn difficult arggg
Food is hard. Like their bread. Carbonara with limited sauce. Drinks like zagu.

Went there today for lunch. Been here 2 times before and the experience was ok and the food was ok. I don't normally write reviews but was pretty upset by the time i left. They screwed up our order and over charged us on items that we have gotten there before. Baked good were so dry we didn't even eat. Like they were made a week ago. Stale and not good at all! I figured we were over charged 600P on stuff. And like I said... extra items we didn't even want. Tried to see if they would make it write but they wouldn't do anything so i paid, and left. Will never go there agian and would recommend you don't either.
nice area, very fit na magchill here. also not that crowded. and love their healthy menu. medyo pricey but i think the food is delicious so worth it.

A bit pricey, but worth the atmosphere and the quality of the food. [Update] The real estate agent of the venue was very pushy. He kept calling during inconvenient times and can't take a hint that we are not interested. Blocked them in the end.
I love the coffee sua da and the cakes are delicious its a little bit pricey compared to other cafes but its worth the price. The place is very relaxing too.

I rate the coffee we order 5.9/10. Food is 5.5/10. Small serving but quite tasty. Lastly the music choice doesn't quite fit the atmosphere of the coffee shop.
